### thm-baire-category-locally-compact-hausdorff — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "for every sequence $(U_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of dense open subsets of $X$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-sequence-convergence-top]]), the intersection $\bigcap_{n \in \mathbb{N}} U_n$ is dense in $X$." "[L6] Assuming dependent choice: if $A$ is nonempty and $(R_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ are relations on $A$ such that every $u \in A$ has some $v \in A$ with $u \mathbin{R_n} v$, then for every $a_0 \in A$ there is $a : \mathbb{N} \to A$ with $a(0) = a_0$ and $a(n) \mathbin{R_n} a(n+1)$ for every $n$ ([[lem-dependent-choice-along-a-sequence-of-relations]], [[def-sequence-convergence-top]], [[def-natural-numbers]])."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. The repaired sequence citation has the right arbitrary-space domain. The stagewise-choice target states dependent choice along a sequence of relations. The local compactness target states that every open set around a point contains an open set with compact closure inside it, and the compactness target states, “A space is compact exactly when every family of closed subsets with the finite intersection property has nonempty intersection.” These are exactly the shrinking and intersection steps used in the proof.

### lem-the-order-topology-on-an-ordinal — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "In an ordinal every point other than a limit is isolated, and the sets $(\alpha,\beta]$ are the convenient basic sets that always stay clopen: an open interval $(\alpha,\beta)$ need not be closed, while $(\alpha,\beta]$ always is, because its complement is again a union of sets of the two admissible forms."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. Calling these sets convenient, rather than the exclusive basic sets, agrees with claim 1, whose basis also contains initial segments. The order-topology target states that the space, open rays, and open intervals form a basis; the present proof correctly refines those sets by clopen initial or half-open intervals. The cited ordinal compactness theorem begins, “Every successor ordinal is compact in its order topology and every limit ordinal is not,” and explicitly invokes this clopen basis.

### thm-the-long-line-is-countably-compact-and-not-compact — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "Every closed initial segment of the long ray is compact; the long ray is not compact; and, assuming countable choice, it is countably compact and not Lindel\\\"of"
ASSESSMENT: The repaired title is correct and now scopes countable choice to both countable compactness and failure of Lindelofness. The item nevertheless has a dependency-direction defect. Fact L6 states only that a nonempty at-most-countable family may be listed. Step 1.3 uses the converse direction to infer that the range of a listed sequence is at most countable. The cited target does contain that converse and says, “This is the working form of countability used everywhere below: to prove a nonempty set countable it suffices to list its elements, repetitions and all.” But L6 does not state that direction, contrary to the required Fact fidelity, so step 1.3 is not licensed by the current stated fact.
COLLATERAL: The title repair broke nothing; the independent L6 direction defect remains.

### thm-quasicomponents-equal-components-in-a-compact-hausdorff-space — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: "Nothing above says the components are open. If every component of $X$ is a singleton then $X$ is totally disconnected, that being the definition; what the theorem adds is that the quasicomponents are then singletons too. Local connectedness is a separate hypothesis, sufficient to make the components open, and openness of the components of $X$ alone is strictly weaker than it ([[thm-components-partition-and-are-closed]])."
ASSESSMENT: The mathematical correction is true, but its citation is not. The cited target is titled “The components of a space are its maximal connected subsets, they partition it, and each of them is closed,” and it says only, “Components need not be open, and no clause above says they are.” It does not state that local connectedness makes components open or that openness of the components of the whole space is strictly weaker. The on-disk result that actually states the needed proposition is titled “A space is locally connected exactly when every component of every open subspace is open; in that case the components of the space itself are clopen.” That target is neither cited nor declared as a dependency.
COLLATERAL: The repaired Remark replaced a false equivalence with a true statement but left the new sufficiency and strictness claims attached to a target that does not make them.
STAMPS: `precheck: pass` only; stale judgment and verification blocks were correctly removed, but a new certification is not warranted.

### rem-compactness-conventions-and-choice-ledger — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "Compactness belongs to $A$ together with its topology. It is preserved under a homeomorphic realization as a subspace, but a different ambient may induce a different topology and a different compactness answer." "The refutations of [[fs-a-compact-subset-is-closed-in-every-space]] and of [[fs-local-compactness-is-hereditary]] are also theorems of ZF: each exhibits a single explicit witness and spends no choice principle." "[[lem-tube-lemma-for-a-compact-factor]] avoids even the finite selection: it indexes its cover by *pairs* of open sets, so the compactness criterion hands back the second entries with the indices. [[thm-compact-subset-of-a-hausdorff-space-is-closed]] avoids the *arbitrary* selection by collecting the family of **all** open sets that work rather than choosing one for each point, and then makes only the finite selections that [[lem-finite-choice]] supplies." "Nothing here supersedes it: by [[thm-compactness-agrees-with-metric-compactness]] for compactness itself, and by the agreement clauses of [[def-compactness-variants]] for countable compactness, sequential compactness and limit point compactness, the metric statements are the statements of this page read in a metric topology."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. The ambient criterion and metric comparison targets state respectively that ambient open covers characterize the fixed subspace topology and that the two notions of compact subset coincide. The finite-choice target is titled “Every natural-number-indexed list of nonempty sets has a choice function on its family of values.” The tube lemma explicitly says no choice principle is used, while the Hausdorff compact-set theorem says its proof uses only finitely many selections after collecting all working open sets. The five false statements are all accounted for: compact-implies-closed and heredity of local compactness have explicit ZF witnesses; compact-implies-sequentially-compact says the Axiom of Choice is assumed; sequentially-compact-implies-compact and countably-compact-implies-compact each say the refutation assumes Countable Choice. Finally, the compactness-variants target expressly says “the condition is the same condition,” “the subsequences quantified over are the same,” and “the same neighbourhood base makes the two conditions one,” exactly licensing the metric-ledger comparison.

### cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology — CERTIFY
CURRENT TEXT READ: "For reals $a_k \le b_k$ the box $\prod_{k<n} [a_k, b_k]$ is a product of finitely many compact spaces, each $[a_k,b_k]$ being compact by claim 2 applied with $n = 1$, so [[thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces]] makes it compact using only the one-dimensional case of claim 2, and with it only the one-dimensional bisection." "\"Bounded\" in claim 2 is a property of the metric $d_2$, not of the topology it induces: a metrizable space with at least two points carries, for every positive real $D$, a compatible metric of diameter $D$."
ASSESSMENT: Correct. The finite-product target states, “A product of finitely many compact spaces is compact in the product topology.” The Heine–Borel target says, “No choice principle is used,” and proves the one-dimensional compactness invoked for each factor by bisection. The diameter assertion is also true: start with any compatible metric, replace it by a bounded compatible transform, and rescale by its positive finite diameter. The at-least-two-points hypothesis is exactly what ensures that diameter is positive. The cited false-statement target confirms that closed and bounded need not imply compactness in an arbitrary metric space.
